findings.title: EventManager is built with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler constructs the EventManager via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) })`, i.e. with the session user's credentials. But the endpoint explicitly allows callers who are not the organizer (team admins/owners and attendees). For those callers the organizer's calendar credential is not present, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` cannot update the calendar event that lives on the organizer's calendar — it will either throw (after the attendees were already persisted, and before any emails are sent, so the user sees an error toast even though the guests were added) or silently skip the update, leaving the new guests off the calendar event. Notably, the booking query already includes `user: { include: { credentials: true } }`, i.e. the organizer's credentials were fetched but never used, which strongly suggests they were the intended source. Use the booking organizer's credentials for the EventManager.

findings.title: Team permission check uses && instead of ||, rejecting team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. A membership has a single role, so an ADMIN who is not OWNER fails this check; and if `isTeamAdmin` already includes OWNER in its role filter, the AND reduces to 'owners only'. As the variable name and the UI (which offers 'Additional guests' to team admins viewing team bookings) imply, this should be an OR. Consequence: team admins who can see the booking on /bookings get a FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' error when adding guests.

findings.title: Guests are persisted before the calendar update, with no rollback or error handling
findings.body: The attendee rows are created via `prisma.booking.update(...)` and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs outside any try/catch. If the calendar call throws (expired credential, provider API error, no matching credential), the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already in the database: no notification emails are sent (that call comes later), and a retry fails with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests now exist. The booking ends up with guests that nobody was notified about and no way to re-trigger the notifications. Wrap the calendar/email side effects so a failure there doesn't masquerade as a failed guest add, or perform them before/atomically with the DB write.

findings.title: No validation of booking status or time before adding guests
findings.body: After fetching the booking, the handler never checks `booking.status` or whether the booking is in the past. The UI only shows the action for upcoming confirmed bookings, but the tRPC endpoint itself can be called directly: an attendee or team admin can add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-past booking. The handler will then create attendee records and send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with a CONFIRMED-status ics REQUEST to arbitrary addresses for an event that is cancelled or over. Add a guard rejecting non-confirmed or past bookings.

findings.title: Input schema enforces neither uniqueness within guests[] nor a maximum length
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` only validates email format. The client dialog checks for duplicate emails, but the tRPC endpoint can be called directly with duplicates: the handler's filter only compares against existing booking attendees, so `createMany` inserts multiple Attendee rows with the same email for one booking, and each duplicate receives its own invitation email. The array is also unbounded, so a single request can fan out invitation emails (with event details and video link) to a very large number of arbitrary addresses. Add a uniqueness refine and a reasonable `.max(...)` to the schema.

findings.title: Guest emails are compared case-sensitively and never normalized, bypassing the blacklist and duplicate checks
findings.body: The dedup/blacklist filter uses raw string equality: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist entries are lowercased (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(',').map(e => e.toLowerCase())`) but the incoming guest is not, so `Blocked@x.com` sails past a `blocked@x.com` blacklist entry. Likewise `John@x.com` is inserted as a second attendee when `john@x.com` is already on the booking. Normalize (lowercase/trim) each guest before the duplicate check, the blacklist check, and persistence.

findings.title: Adding guests to seated event types bypasses seat capacity and seat records
findings.body: For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, attendees normally get BookingSeat/seat references and capacity is enforced. This handler inserts the new guests as plain Attendee rows via `createMany` with no seat bookkeeping and no capacity check, so a seated booking can be overbooked beyond `seatsPerTimeSlot`, and the added guests lack the seat references that seat-based flows (attendee reschedule/cancel via seatReferenceUid) rely on. Either reject seated bookings in this mutation or create proper seat records and enforce capacity.

findings.title: Raw `guests` input (not `uniqueGuests`) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original request input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, any attendee whose email appears in `newGuests` gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a brand-new 'booking confirmed' email with ics REQUEST) instead of the 'guests added' notification. So if the request redundantly included an email that was filtered out because that person is already an attendee, that existing attendee is incorrectly emailed as if they had just booked. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send function here (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.host` / `.attendee`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees, so organizers who explicitly disabled standard emails for an event type will still trigger these 'guests added' and scheduling emails. Thread the event type metadata through and gate host/attendee emails like the other functions.

findings.title: Bookings without an owner user (dynamic bookings) crash with a 500
findings.body: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws Prisma's NotFound error for bookings where `userId` is null (e.g. dynamic collective bookings), surfacing as an unhandled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a clean client error. This path is reachable: for such bookings `isOrganizer` is false but an attendee passes the `isAttendee` check, then the handler 500s. Handle the missing-organizer case explicitly.

findings.title: Email failures are swallowed and reported as success
findings.body: `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) } catch (err) { console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') }` discards the actual error (it's not logged) and lets the mutation return success, so the user sees a 'Guests added' toast even when none of the notification/invitation emails were sent. At minimum log the error object via the standard logger, and consider surfacing the partial failure to the caller.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail flag is not reset on success, so a stale error banner reappears on reopen
findings.body: The dialog component stays mounted (visibility is toggled via the `open` prop), so its state persists between opens. `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` but never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. If a user triggers the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error, then fixes the input and submits successfully, the red error banner is still set and will be visible the next time the dialog is opened, above a fresh empty input. Reset `isInvalidEmail` in `onSuccess` (and ideally whenever the dialog closes).

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation with non-trivial authorization (organizer vs team admin vs team owner vs attendee vs stranger), input filtering (duplicates, blacklist), and side effects (calendar update, emails), but no tests. The permission bug alone (`isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` instead of an OR) and the duplicate-guest handling would have been caught by even a basic permission-matrix and input-validation test.
